13 A uniform rod is attached by a hinge at one end to a wall. The other end of the rod is supported
by a wire so that the rod is horizontal and in equilibrium.
wire
wall
hinge
rod
Which arrow shows the direction of the force on the rod from the hinge?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the wire is diagonal from the wall down to the right end, so its tension on the rod pulls up and to the left.
For horizontal equilibrium the hinge must provide a horizontal component to the right to cancel the leftward pull of the wire.
For vertical equilibrium and zero moment about the hinge, the hinge must also push upward to help support half the weight of the rod.
walkthrough: List the forces on the horizontal rod: weight $W$ down at the centre, tension $T$ along the wire up and to the left at the right end, and hinge force $H$ at the left end.
Resolve the tension: it has an upward component $T_y$ and a leftward component $T_x$ because the wire slopes down to the right.
Take moments about the hinge for equilibrium: $T_y \times L = W \times L/2$, so $T_y = W/2$ upward, leaving an upward force still needed.
Balance vertical forces: $H_y + T_y - W = 0$, so $H_y = W - W/2$ upward on the rod.
Balance horizontal forces: $H_x - T_x = 0$, so $H_x = T_x$ to the right on the rod.
Combine $H_x$ to the right with $H_y$ upward to give a hinge force directed up and to the right. This is option D.

A.explanation: Purely vertical upward ignores the horizontal pull of the angled wire on the right end of the rod.

B.explanation: Downward cannot balance the downward weight when the wire already pulls upward on the rod.

C.explanation: Up and to the left adds to the leftward component of the wire tension, so horizontal forces cannot balance.

D.explanation: Up and to the right balances the downward weight and the leftward component of the angled wire tension.
